items.title: 66960_Gil Evans oral history interview
items.q: So Lionel was with Benny Goodman, so was Teddy Wilson and a trumpet player... Bunny Berigan in.

ctx.x: Well Benny Goodman fell into the mood of those at the time. It's very hard to describe to anybody now what Benny Goodman was like in 1935. At that time he had a lot of fire and a tone on the clarinet which he (tone they were trying to reach?). Later changed to a legitimate tone which he has now. And what he plays with his jazz band now don't sound like nothing because he doesn't have that tone, that he had. So he fit in well with it. It wasn't as though he was like something removed from Fletcher's arrangements.…
